summary: Order placement 500s are caused by dep-5101, order-service v2.14.0 (deployed 2026-03-03T12:10:00Z), which added a new MarginCheckValidator that throws NullPointerException ("marginProfile is null") for futures & options orders, returning HTTP 500 on POST /v1/orders while equity orders are unaffected. The deploy is the only order-service change in the window and the latest change fleet-wide, landing ~2.5 minutes before the first matching error log at 12:12:31Z and the first elevated error bucket at 12:12. Confidence is high (0.88, capped by the Critic). The strongest rival explanation — a shared-platform fault (ledger-db/kafka/redis) — is positively discriminated: all three other ledger-db consumers (portfolio-, payment-, settlement-service) stayed flat at ~0.21% error rate through the onset buckets, and order-service latency/pool metrics were flat, indicating a fail-fast code defect rather than saturation. Residual uncertainty concerns secondary mechanism detail (in-process vs. outbound null source) and the absence-of-evidence basis for non-FNO unaffectedness, not which origin to fix.

ranked_hypotheses.title: dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0) added MarginCheckValidator which NPEs on F&O orders
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The only fleet-wide deployment, order-service v2.14.0 (dep-5101, 12:10:00Z), replaced legacy OrderRules.validateMargin() with a new MarginCheckValidator. The new validator dereferences a margin profile that is null for futures & options accounts (the legacy path tolerated or derived it), so every F&O order reaching validation throws NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.java:88 and POST /v1/orders returns 500 for derivatives while equity orders stay healthy.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5101 deploys order-service v2.14.0 at 12:10:00Z: 'Refactor order validation; add margin check for F&O orders' — adds new MarginCheckValidator, removes legacy OrderRules.validateMargin()
The new validator executes for F&O (orderType=FNO) orders and dereferences a marginProfile that is null for those accounts, throwing NPE at MarginCheckValidator.java:88
The unhandled NPE is mapped to HTTP 500 by the order API ('order rejected with 500: marginProfile is null for account')
Because the new code only governs the derivatives/F&O validation branch, failures are scoped to orderType=FNO; all 224 logged errors are FNO and no non-FNO order type appears
Onset ordering: deploy 12:10:00Z -> first NPE log 12:12:31Z -> error rate jumps in the 12:12 bucket; healthy (0.13-0.23%) in the 12:08-12:11 buckets
Failure is fail-fast, not a latency/dependency/timeout pattern: latency_p99 flat ~150ms and db_pool_in_use flat ~14 across the window
Elevated rate is sustained (17.97% -> 18.85% at 13:58) and request volume did not change, so it is a rate change not a traffic change
Blast radius attenuates correctly upstream: api-gateway error_rate rises only to ~3.3-3.5%, consistent with just the order route failing

assumptions: The null marginProfile originates in-process from the new validator's own handling (missing/absent account margin snapshot for FNO) rather than from an outbound lookup that started returning null; no trace/span data resolved the failing span.
No code-level diff/version history is available beyond the deploy summary; the exact line 88 semantics are inferred from the matched log pattern.

No direct telemetry was obtained for ledger-db/kafka/redis/pricing-engine/exchange-gateway; their health at 12:10Z is accepted based on the absence of any recorded change plus the unaffected co-consumers (F20-F22).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared platform dependency (ledger-db / kafka / redis-cache) faults around 12:10-12:22Z and surfaces as order-service 500s
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A fault in a shared component on the order path (ledger-db postgres, kafka, or redis-cache reachable via pricing-engine) degrades or returns errors/nulls to order-service, which surfaces this as marginProfile-is-null NPEs and HTTP 500s. If true, the same failure should appear in the other consumers of the shared component.

causal_chain.claim: order-service writes directly to ledger-db, reaches redis-cache via pricing-engine, and produces to kafka; all three are shared platform components
ledger-db is shared by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service, so a ledger-db fault would surface as 500s across all four consumers

Blast-radius test FAILS: all three other ledger-db consumers are flat through 11:30-13:59Z (portfolio-service mean 0.21%, payment-service mean 0.21%, settlement-service mean 0.21%, with the 12:12/12:19 onset buckets at 0.20-0.26%) — no simultaneous degradation
Fault must originate in order-service, not the shared datastore

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Ruled out by blast radius, the exact discriminator the critique identified: portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service — the three other ledger-db consumers — show flat ~0.21% error rates across the whole 11:30-13:59Z window including the 12:12/12:19 onset buckets (F20, F21, F22). A ledger-db origin would have failed all four consumers simultaneously. Additionally, the observed failure is a deterministic code NPE on a derivatives-only branch introduced by dep-5101 (F10, F29), not a datastore/cache null-return pattern; no shared component has any recorded change (F18); order-service latency/pool metrics are flat (F12); and no precedent matches (F19).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Off-path config change / misconfiguration (cfg-2101 or an order-service profile override) caused the failures
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A configuration change rather than code introduced the failure — e.g. cfg-2101 raising notification-service email.batch_size, or an order-service config/profile override in the historical HIST-115 connection-pool pattern. This is only viable if a config on the order path had changed.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2101 changed notification-service email.batch_size 200→250 at 11:21Z — the only config change in the fleet in the window
notification-service is not on the order path, so its config change cannot produce order-service 500s (blast radius excludes it)
order-service had zero config changes in the 24h window, ruling out a profile/flag override (HIST-115 pattern)

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: cfg-2101 is on notification-service, which is off the order path, so it cannot produce order-service 500s (F16); order-service itself had zero config changes in the 24h window (F17), removing the profile/flag-override HIST-115 pattern; and the error signature is a code-level NPE in a validator introduced by a deployment (F10), not a pool-exhaustion signature.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Overload / resource exhaustion in order-service or a shared component caused intermittent null-profile handling and 500s
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The error spike is a symptom of saturation (pool exhausted, throttled IOPS, cold-cache storm) rather than a code defect: under pressure a margin/portfolio lookup times out or returns incomplete state, so order-service raises null marginProfile errors. Historical precedents HIST-110 (ledger-db IOPS throttling) and HIST-107 (cold cache storm) are the anchors.

causal_chain.claim: Historical precedents exist for order failures driven by ledger-db IOPS throttling and by redis cold-cache storms after failover
Under such pressure a margin/profile lookup would return null or time out, producing the NPE/500 — speculative; no such error signature in those precedents, and latency/pool metrics are flat
order-service latency_p99 stayed flat ~147-153ms and db_pool_in_use flat ~14 connections across the window

assumptions: Saturation could exist in a component whose error metrics were never queried, and could manifest as null rather than timeout errors.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: order-service latency_p99 stayed flat at ~147-153ms and db_pool_in_use flat at ~14 connections across the window (F12, F24), i.e. no saturation signal; the failure mode is fail-fast (latency flat while errors spike), the opposite of saturation; the dominant signature is a deterministic code NPE in a validator introduced by dep-5101 (F9, F10); no shared component's consumers show degradation (F20-F22); and the cited precedents are leads only, none matching this signature (F19).

Request volume did not change at onset (request_rate ~224-236 req/s across 12:00-12:20), so the 5xx jump is a rate change, not a traffic change.

The only other degradation is at the caller: api-gateway error_rate went from ~0.2% (12:00/12:06 buckets) to ~3.37% at 12:12 and stayed ~3.3-3.5% through 13:48 — consistent with a subset of gateway traffic (the order route) failing rather than an independent origin.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0) to the previous version and confirm the error rate returns to baseline; since the deploy removed legacy OrderRules.validateMargin() and added MarginCheckValidator, rollback restores the legacy margin path that tolerated/derived the absent FNO margin profile.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-5101 is the only order-service change and the latest fleet change, landing ~2.5 minutes before the first matching NPE; the failure is fail-fast and sustained, and rollback is the lowest-risk mitigation.

recommended_actions.action: If rollback is not immediately possible, disable/feature-flag the MarginCheckValidator F&O branch in the order-service validation chain so FNO orders fall back to the prior margin handling.
recommended_actions.rationale: The NPE is deterministic on the new validator at MarginCheckValidator.java:88 for orderType=FNO, so bypassing that branch should stop the 500s for derivatives orders while a proper fix is prepared.

recommended_actions.action: After rollback/disablement, verify recovery on order-service error_rate (expect return to ~0.2-0.3%) and confirm api-gateway error rate falls back toward ~0.2%, while portfolio-/payment-/settlement-service remain flat.
recommended_actions.rationale: Recovery after removing dep-5101's new validator is the decisive confirmation of H1; the current data contains no rollback event to validate against (rolled_back_at null).

recommended_actions.action: Fix MarginCheckValidator to null-safe the marginProfile path for FNO accounts (derive or default the margin profile as the legacy OrderRules.validateMargin() path did) and add unit/integration coverage for FNO accounts with an absent margin snapshot before redeploying.
recommended_actions.rationale: The root defect is a null dereference on the FNO branch; the legacy path tolerated or derived the null margin profile, so the replacement must preserve that behaviour.

recommended_actions.action: Add per-order-type / per-endpoint error-rate and request-rate dimensions to order-service metrics so non-FNO (equity) health can be positively measured rather than inferred from absence of error logs.
recommended_actions.rationale: order-service exposes only service-wide metrics and logs carry no non-FNO order lines, so non-FNO unaffectedness currently rests on absence-of-evidence rather than a computed failure rate — this is the main residual cap on confidence.

recommended_actions.action: Add a canary/staged rollout with automatic error-rate abort for order-service deploys, and expand shared-component telemetry (ledger-db, kafka, redis-cache) to expose error/latency series for faster future blast-radius discrimination.
recommended_actions.rationale: The deploy's impact was visible within one minute of going live, but no canary gate stopped it; and the shared components expose no error series, which forced H2 to be excluded indirectly via consumer error rates.

what_would_change_the_conclusion: Rollback of dep-5101 not reducing order-service error rate (or the NPE continuing after rollback) would overturn H1 and refocus attention on a shared-component or another origin.

Simultaneous error-rate degradation in portfolio-service, payment-service and/or settlement-service at 12:12/12:19 would revive H2 (shared ledger-db/platform fault) and contradict H1's blast-radius discrimination.
Evidence that FNO orders reached MarginCheckValidator before dep-5101 (e.g. pre-deploy NPEs or an earlier FNO margin check path) would break the temporal/causal chain.

Evidence of a null-returning outbound lookup (e.g. traces showing a margin/portfolio dependency returning null, or a change to such a dependency) would shift the mechanism away from in-process null handling and possibly the origin/fix.
A feature-flag/canary showing dep-5101's MarginCheckValidator was not actually active on the failing traffic path would break the causal chain.
Evidence that equity (non-FNO) orders were also failing at a comparable rate would contradict the derivatives-only scoping that the mechanism relies on.

Latency/saturation degradation in order-service or a shared component (e.g. db_pool_in_use exhaustion, redis evictions, kafka under-replicated partitions) would support H4 and undermine the fail-fast code-defect conclusion.

Request volume did not change at onset, so the 5xx jump is a rate change not a traffic change: request_rate stays ~224-236 req/s across 12:00-12:20 (12:10 avg 230.01, 12:12 avg 232.61, 12:14 avg 235.57).

Order-type scoping: a full-range scan of order-service ERROR logs for 'orderType=' returned total_matched 224, all ERROR, all of the single pattern 'NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.validate(MarginCheckValidator.java:<n>) orderType=FNO orderId=<n>' — zero occurrences of any non-FNO orderType in the error stream.

Non-FNO orders are not merely filtered from the error view but absent from order-service logs altogether: an INFO-or-higher scan for 'equity' over 12:05-13:59Z returned total_matched 0 (data_range 08:00-13:59Z, not truncated), so there is no per-order-type INFO logging and no non-FNO denominator available in logs.

Blast radius reaches the caller but attenuated: api-gateway error_rate is 0.19-0.20% in the 12:00 and 12:06 buckets, then 3.37% at 12:12 and stays ~3.3-3.5% through 13:48 — consistent with a subset of gateway traffic (the order route) failing rather than the gateway itself. Sparse 360s buckets here (available_metrics for api-gateway has no db_pool_in_use), so gateway onset is bounded to 12:06-12:12, not sub-minute.
